newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - July 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - July 15.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, now attending a UNESCO seminar in germany, has called upon the world community to launch a concerted drive to free the developing countries from illiteracy.
The deadline for submission of proposals to participate in the bidding for hydrocarbon exploration in the country's 15 free blocks expires on Tuesday.
The river Ganges continued to swell on Monday, inundating fresh areas in some northern and southwestern districts.
Police has prepared a list of "godfathers" who allegedly patronise notorious terrorists in the capital city.
Bangladesh government has appealed to the United Nations High Commissioners for Refugees (UNHCR) to help repatriate Bangladeshi nationals from Cambodia.
Former President Hussain Muhammad Ershad left Dhaka for Saudi Arabia on Monday for treatment.
Thr government is going to float a number of schemes to mobilise funds for the industrial sector, Finance Minister S.A.M.S. Kibria said.
The newly appointed chairman of the Securities & Exchange Commission, Abu Sayeed, will formally join his office on Wednesday. REUTER
